quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: This sign means you are approaching a railroad crossing without signals. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, you must slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop. Never try to drive faster than an approaching train.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the centerline to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Something that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is a major cause of accidents because it makes drivers miss important sights and sounds.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When you see a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, you can pass from the broken line side only. The solid line side cannot pass.

questions.question: Traffic on the freeway is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Drive faster to protect your right-of-way.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When safe, you should make room to allow other vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction if you are in the right lane and the road is clear. This is true even when a red light is showing.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. It is unsafe and against the law to turn right here.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, you should be able to see:

options.text: The entire rear window.
The passengers in the back seat.
Your own face.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire rear window.
questions.explanation: Adjust your rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window. You should only move your eyes, not your head, to use this mirror.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass them slowly at 10 mph or less.
Stop and only go when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only go when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. You cannot see pedestrians who may be crossing. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed before going.

questions.question: You are approaching a yellow traffic light and have not entered the intersection yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Slow down and go through carefully.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are not already in the intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection, go through quickly.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor how it will affect your driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor how it will affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Medicine can affect your driving ability. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving if you take any medicine. This is especially important for tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when it first rains. On a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops.
Test your tire traction by driving uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid fast turns and stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is blocking your way.
It may help prevent a crash.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when needed to avoid crashes. Do not use it to make slow drivers go faster or move out of your way.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: On the highway, looking far ahead helps you:

options.text: Keep up with traffic.
Avoid sudden braking or turning.
Spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead to avoid sudden stops or lane changes. This helps you drive safely, save fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street to:

options.text: See hazards early.
Account for long stopping distances.
Keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: See hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes ahead. Watch for signals from other drivers. Prepare for merging vehicles and sudden road or traffic changes.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using only your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you spot vehicles that mirrors may not show.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane with oncoming traffic ahead. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If visibility is too poor, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive through the intersection without stopping.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to fully cross the tracks.
When the railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When you are driving with two or more young children in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to fully cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, going either direction. Always make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks ahead
Trucks must use second gear
Steep hill ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: A bad suspension system can cause:

options.text: Problems controlling your vehicle.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Problems controlling your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and makes the ride smooth. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.
